A third run gave 5.26 M `surface_before` calls on 440,807 distinct samples, 172.7 s.

## What dominates in these numbers

Tangency is not the main cost: it is 3.9 s in release. 98 percent of the time is in `Rest::surface_before`, at about 34 microseconds a call. Each call runs `island_threshold` (a binary search of about 16 `island_holds`) and then `clears` on the near chords. Each `island_holds` is a full `Region::contains` over a slice of some thousands of edges. The call count is high because the ramp puts the wall samples of about 1,700 planes in each band disc at the 8 dead ends, and about 300 ramp moves read the same discs.

## Notes for the fix

- `surface_before` reads a slice at the plane of each near chord, not only at the sample planes. A smaller sample plane set reduces the calls, but the column law still slices every cut Z.
- An exact option, not measured and not pushed: a Y-slab index on each cached slice. It reads only the edges whose Y range holds `q.y`, with the same arithmetic in the same order, so it gives `Region::contains` bit for bit. It removes most of the cost per call and drops no sample.
- A sample plane set of "cut levels plus the deepest cut" is not exact for a ramp along a sloped or curved wall: the section of a ramp plane stands at its own place, and its wall samples then leave the set. The equivalence pin must use such a wall, not only vertical walls.

Note for the fix of this issue, from the coordinator (the measurement is in the comment above). Two facts decide the review of the PR: (1) in release, 98 percent of the time is `Rest::surface_before` in `band_reach` (about 154 s to 174 s for one generation); tangency is 3.9 s. (2) A plane set of "the cut levels plus the deepest cut" removes the samples of the ramp planes. On a sloped or curved wall the section of each ramp plane is at a different place, so a shank verdict can change. A missed shank hit is a `P1` class result. The review will ask for an equivalence pin against the current code on a ramp along a sloped wall and along a curved wall (same warnings, same order), as #3595 did. An exact alternative is named above: a point-location index on each cached slice that gives the same result as `Region::contains`.

blocked: the levels-plus-deepest plane set is not verdict-equivalent.

Finding, from the existing sloped ramp fixture `ramp_at(500, 36.0)`:
- The all-plane reference convicts `ShankHit { part: true }` at moves 250 to 292 and 293 to 329.
- The new levels-plus-deepest set convicts moves 250 to 273 and 293 to 329.
- The new set loses moves 274 to 292. That is 19 part-true convictions.

The lost moves are real collisions. The shank bottom stands below the boss top Z 10. Its rim reaches 1 mm into the boss wall, and the flute did not clear that wall point. The per-chord planes also place triangulation-tie wall vertices at z-dependent positions. One plane cannot reproduce them.

The change stops at the equivalence gate (condition 4). The proof pin `verify::reach_tests::a_many_plane_ramp_reads_only_the_samples_near_its_discs` fails on purpose. I did not adjust the fixture and I did not weaken the reference.

The speed result is real. On the away-from-wall ramp `ramp_at(2000, 34)`, slices fall from 2000 to 1 and sample_tests from 32,016,000 to 0.

Held work: branch `issue/3615-verify-cut-levels`, draft PR #3620 (do not merge). The full record is in `docs/decisions/3615-verify-cut-levels.md`.

A fix needs a plane set that keeps the wall points the per-chord planes give. That is a new design.

The failed plane-set attempt is recorded, and it sets the bar for the next two designs. Each of them must carry the SAME equivalence proof: on sloped and stepped fixtures, every verdict (gouge/no-gouge, reach counts, findings) is identical to the pre-change code, and a pinned comparison fails if one verdict moves. The 19 lost `ShankHit{part:true}` collisions at moves 274-292 of `ramp_at(500, 36.0)` are the evidence that the proof is not optional.

Candidate designs and their trade-off:

- (a) Memoise `Rest::surface_before` per plane. This keeps every plane and every verdict by construction, and it attacks the measured hotspot: in release about 98 percent of the time is `Rest::surface_before` in `band_reach` (about 154 s to 174 s for one generation; tangency 3.9 s). Risk: memory (one cache entry per plane; ~1,700 planes here) and cache invalidation correctness. The proof is still required - the memo must return byte-identical surfaces.
- (b) Bound the sample count another way that provably keeps every plane's findings. This keeps the plane set but reduces the work per plane (for example an exact XY index per plane, a conservative sample expansion, or an incremental section per plane). Risk: a bound that is not conservative drops a collision, which is the failure this attempt showed. The proof is the same.

Neither design may merge without the equivalence pin over the sloped and stepped fixtures and the reached heavy sim/verify lanes on them.
